fields.meta_description: Take a 7-question quiz funnel that names the funnel your business needs, then build one that scores leads and saves answers. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Quiz Funnel That Turns Answers Into Leads
fields.hero_description: Take the 7-question quiz funnel below, or build a quiz funnel that scores answers and saves every lead to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: From the First Question to a Lead Record
fields.features_subheading: A quiz funnel asks a few questions and gives each visitor something personal back. Emergent builds the quiz and its lead table.
fields.feature_1:
Results written before the questions

Name the results you want, such as three service packages. Emergent writes questions that point to them and the logic that picks one, and a follow-up prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
A score with the cutoff you choose

Give each answer points and set a cutoff. A lead at or above it goes to your sales rep by email or Slack with every answer attached, and everyone below it still sees their result.
fields.feature_3:
The email ask where you want it

Ask for an email before the result, after it, or not at all. Each finished quiz becomes a row in a database you own, holding the answers, the score, and the result it reached.
fields.feature_4:
Leads sent to the CRM you already use

A finished quiz can create a lead in HubSpot or any CRM with an API, tagged with the result it reached. Your sales rep opens that record and reads every answer before the first call.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Visitors answer one question per screen on a phone, with a progress bar across the top showing how many questions are left. Emergent puts no cap on how many people take the quiz.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, with the code in GitHub

Host the quiz on your own domain, included in Emergent and paid in credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository. The free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.usecase_heading: Quiz Funnels at Work in Four Businesses
fields.tab_content_1:
Rafe hears about every score of 8 or more

Homeowners on Sunreach Solar's site answer 6 questions on roof age, shade, and the electric bill, scored from 0 to 10. Ione Gundersby scores 9, over the cutoff of 8, so sales rep Rafe Hollinger gets an email with her 6 answers. Her lead and score are saved to Sunreach's lead table.
fields.tab_content_2:
Behind on books, sent to Catch-Up Cleanup

Bettina Lusk, who runs a cafe, tells Penwick Bookkeeping's quiz that 9 months of statements are unreconciled, and it matches her to Catch-Up Cleanup. Her result page shows the $1,500 starting price above a callback request for her name and phone number. The request lands in Penwick's lead table with her answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 252 Light results get the Light series

In March, 600 people finished Glasshour Photo School's quiz on what holds their photos back, each giving an email first. It sorted 252 into Light, 198 into Framing, and 150 into Editing. The app tags every finisher in the school's email tool through its API, and the 252 Light results get the Light email series.
fields.tab_content_4:
When budget sat at question 4, 260 people quit

Pike Mill Kitchens watched its quiz funnel through September: 1,800 people started and 1,170 finished. Its drop-off report showed that 260 of the 630 who quit left at question 4, the budget question. The owner moved budget to the last screen, after the questions on room and layout.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Quiz Funnel
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a quiz funnel that sends every result to a next step and shows where people quit.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the offer behind each result
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the results before the questions
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Cut it to 8 questions or fewer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide where the email ask goes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with what you sell, not with questions. List up to 4 offers a visitor could end up with, such as a service package, a course track, or a call with sales. Every result in the quiz should point to exactly one of them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each result a name a visitor would be glad to get, two sentences on why it fits them, and one next step. Questions come faster once every option has a result to point at, and none of them lead nowhere.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask only what changes the result or what your sales rep needs before the first call. Drop any question whose answers all point the same way. Put easy questions first, and save anything personal, like budget, for the last screens.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the email ask before the result when the follow-up series is the point of the funnel. Put it after the result when the result page itself makes the offer. Ask for a phone number only when someone on your team will call it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Score the answers that predict a sale
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give points to answers your sales rep cares about, such as roof age for a solar installer, and leave the rest unscored. After the first 50 leads, ask the rep which ones were worth the call, and move the cutoff up or down by 1 point.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with 5 people on their phones
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have 5 people who match your customers take the quiz on a phone while you watch. Note where they pause, then read their result back to them. When a result does not sound like them, rewrite the question that sent them there.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the drop-off report each month
fields.howto_step_7_des: Compare starts with quits at each question once a month. A question that loses far more people than its neighbors is the one to move or cut. Change it with a prompt, then check the next month's finish count against this month's.

faq_plan.a: A quiz funnel is a short quiz that asks a visitor a few questions and gives them something personal in return, such as a matched package or a score. The answers and contact details become a lead, and the result decides what the visitor sees next.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up quiz funnel?
faq_plan.a: Describe the results and where each lead should go, and Emergent's AI survey builder builds the quiz, its scoring, and the lead table from that prompt. Add a CRM sync or a drop-off report with a follow-up prompt, then publish it on your own domain.

faq_plan.q: Why would a business use a lead generation quiz instead of a plain form?
faq_plan.a: Because a lead generation quiz gives the visitor something before it asks for anything: a result or a match. A plain form only asks. The quiz also hands your sales rep each lead's answers, and the first call can start from what the person already said.

faq_plan.q: What are some quiz funnel examples for a small business?
faq_plan.a: Good quiz funnel examples end on something the business sells. A boutique runs a style quiz that closes on the pieces tagged with the shopper's style. A tutoring center places each student in a class, and a landscaper sorts yards into maintenance plans with a monthly price.

faq_plan.q: How do I build a quiz funnel template for my own offers?
faq_plan.a: List your offers first, then describe them in a prompt, and Emergent drafts a quiz funnel template around them: the results, the questions that point to each one, and the lead table. Start from your offers rather than a stock quiz, whose results were written for someone else's products. Change any question later by prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a law firm use a quiz funnel for client intake?
faq_plan.a: It can, if the quiz only sorts the matter and leaves every legal judgment to an attorney. Ask which practice area the matter falls under, when it happened, and how soon the person needs help. Then send the lead to the right attorney, with a consultation request as the result.

faq_plan.q: Can a quiz with right and wrong answers work as a quiz funnel?
faq_plan.hint: How to make a quiz funnel in clickfunnels?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the score points to an offer. A tutoring company can run a vocabulary quiz whose score band picks the course level, then show that course on the result page. Check every correct answer against a source before launch, because visitors will check it too.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a quiz funnel have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 6 to 8 questions: enough to tell your results apart, and short enough to finish on a phone in one sitting. On Emergent, each answer is saved to a database you own. Count the quits at each question, then move or cut the one that loses people.

faq_plan.q: What should a quiz funnel result page include?
faq_plan.a: A result page needs the result's name, two or three sentences on why the answers led there, and one next step tied to an offer, such as a package price or a callback request. Leave out a second offer. If you asked for an email first, say what the follow-up emails will cover.

faq_plan.q: Should a quiz funnel live on its own page or on my website?
faq_plan.a: Give it its own page when paid ads send the traffic, and build a lead generation landing page around the quiz with nothing else to click. Embed it on your site when visitors already arrive there. Either way, Emergent hosts it on your domain, and every lead lands in a database you own.

results.title: A Scored Lead Funnel
results.description: Your answers lean toward a scored lead funnel. Each answer adds points, and a cutoff decides who your sales rep calls first. Leads above it reach the rep by email with every answer attached, and everyone else still sees a result. Score only the answers that predict a sale.

results.title: A Product Finder Funnel
results.description: Your answers lean toward a product finder funnel. Each option maps to a set of items you tag in your catalog, and the result page shows the ones that fit. Keep it to 6 or 7 questions about taste, size, and use, and save each result with the shopper's email for the next newsletter.

results.title: An Email Series Funnel
results.description: Your answers lean toward an email series funnel. The quiz sorts each visitor into one of a few results, asks for an email before showing it, and tags them in your email tool, so each result starts its own series. Write the first email of each series before the questions.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Quiz Funnel That Turns Answers Into Leads'; hero 'build a quiz funnel that scores answers and saves every lead to a database you own'; how-to description says what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is quiz funnel software and examples: page has four worked examples, a quiz funnel template answer (FAQ 5), quiz funnel examples (FAQ 4), a 7-step how-to and a playable 7-question matching quiz.

specificity.evidence: Solar cutoff of 8, Catch-Up Cleanup at $1,500, 252 Light results, 260 of 630 quits at the budget question.

openers.evidence: Every feature body opens on a sentence: 'Name the results you want', 'Give each answer points and set a cutoff'.

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending on the page (tab 1); sentences vary; notes only.

voice.evidence: 'Start with what you sell, not with questions.' Plain, operator voice throughout.

truth.evidence: FAQ 7 'because visitors will check it too' is an unsourced statement of what a type of person does; FAQ 3 'gives the visitor something before it asks for anything' contradicts the page's own email-first funnel (feature 3, how-to 4, tab 3, quiz result 'series').

distinct.evidence: Funnel-specific: score cutoff, drop-off report, offer-first results; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered in the first sentence; hub link in item 2; links to style quiz, vocabulary quiz, lead generation landing page.
